questions.q: To whom did Jeremiah speak Yahweh’s message?
questions.a: He spoke it to all the Jews living in Egypt, in Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and the land of Pathros.

questions.q: Why does Jeremiah say Yahweh brought disaster on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah?
questions.a: Jeremiah says Yahweh did it because the people worshiped other gods.

questions.q: What had Yahweh’s prophets said to the people?
questions.a: The prophets had told the people not to do the detestable thing that Yahweh hates.

questions.q: What did the people do after the prophets spoke to them?
questions.a: They did not listen.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do when the Judeans did not listen to the prophets?
questions.a: Yahweh became very angry and punished them, and the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem became a ruin.

questions.q: How many of the people who went to Egypt will Yahweh allow to live?
questions.a: He says that none of them will be left, including the men, women, children, and infants.

questions.q: How did they make Yahweh angry?
questions.a: They made Yahweh angry by burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say is going to happen to them in Egypt?
questions.a: He says they will destroy themselves, and people in every nation will use their name in curses and despise them.

questions.q: Who does Yahweh say has committed wickedness?
questions.a: He says that the people, their ancestors, the kings of Judah, and their wives have all done evil.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say the people have not done to this day?
questions.a: They have not humbled themselves, shown respect to Yahweh, or obeyed his law.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say will happen to the people who went to Egypt?
questions.a: Yahweh says that he has decided to bring disaster on them and destroy all of Judah. The people who went to Egypt will die there by the sword and by famine.

questions.q: How does Yahweh say he will punish the people living in Egypt?
questions.a: He will punish them with the sword, famine, and plague, just as he punished Jerusalem.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about the remnant of Judah?
questions.a: He says that none of them will escape or live to return to Judah, though they want to return. Only a few will escape from Egypt.

questions.q: Who answered Jeremiah?
questions.a: All the men who knew that their wives were burning incense to other gods, all the women standing nearby, and all the people living in Pathros answered him.

questions.q: What did the people say about the message Jeremiah spoke in the name of Yahweh?
questions.a: They said they would not listen to it.

questions.q: What did the people think would happen if they continued to burn incense and pour out drink offerings to the Queen of Heaven?
questions.a: The people thought they would have plenty of food and prosper, without experiencing any disaster, if they burned incense and poured out drink offerings to the Queen of Heaven.

questions.q: What did the people say happened after they stopped burning incense to the Queen of Heaven?
questions.a: They said that they lacked everything and that many of them died by the sword and by famine.

questions.q: What did the women say about their husbands when they made cakes and poured out drink offerings to the Queen of Heaven?
questions.a: They said that their husbands knew about it and agreed.

questions.q: To whom did Jeremiah speak?
questions.a: He spoke to all the people, both the men and the women, who had answered him.

questions.q: What does Jeremiah say Yahweh did about the incense that the people burned?
questions.a: Jeremiah says Yahweh remembered it and kept thinking about it.

questions.q: What was it that Yahweh could no longer bear?
questions.a: He could no longer bear the people’s evil deeds and the detestable things they did.

questions.q: What happened to their land after Yahweh could no longer bear what the people did?
questions.a: Their land became a ruin, a horror, and a curse, and no one lived there.

questions.q: Why did this disaster happen to them?
questions.a: The disaster happened because they burned incense, sinned against Yahweh, did not listen to him, and did not obey his law.

questions.q: Whom did Jeremiah tell to listen to the word of Yahweh?
questions.a: He told all the people of Judah who were in Egypt, including all the women, to listen.

questions.q: What did Jeremiah tell those who wanted to fulfill their vows to the Queen of Heaven?
questions.a: He told them to fulfill their vows.

questions.q: What did Jeremiah say the people would do after they fulfilled their vows?
questions.a: He told them that no one from Judah in Egypt would ever again use Yahweh’s name to make a promise, and that they would all die by the sword and by famine.

questions.q: What will happen to those who do not die by the sword?
questions.a: A small number of them will return from Egypt to the land of Judah.

questions.q: What will the people know from the sign that Yahweh gives them?
questions.a: They will know that Yahweh’s words about bringing disaster on them will certainly come true.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do with Pharaoh Hophra?
questions.a: He says he will give Pharaoh Hophra to his enemies, who want to kill him, just as he gave Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar.

commentary.text: The Jews in Egypt persist in idolatry. (Jer. 44:1-14) They refuse to reform. (Jer. 44:15-19) Jeremiah then denounces destruction upon them. (Jer. 44:20-30)

Jer. 44:1-14 God reminds the Jews of the sins that brought desolations upon Judah. It becomes us to warn men of the danger of sin with all seriousness: Oh, do not do it! If you love God, do not, for it is provoking to him; if you love your own souls, do not, for it is destructive to them. Let conscience do this for us in the hour of temptation. The Jews whom God sent into the land of the Chaldeans, were there, by the power of God's grace, weaned from idolatry; but those who went by their own perverse will into the land of the Egyptians, were there more attached than ever to their idolatries. When we thrust ourselves without cause or call into places of temptation, it is just with God to leave us to ourselves. If we walk contrary to God, he will walk contrary to us. The most awful miseries to which men are exposed, are occasioned by the neglect of offered salvation.

Jer. 44:15-19 These daring sinners do not attempt excuses, but declare they will do that which is forbidden. Those who disobey God, commonly grow worse and worse, and the heart is more hardened by the deceitfulness of sin. Here is the real language of the rebellious heart. Even the afflictions which should have parted them from their sins, were taken so as to confirm them in their sins. It is sad when those who should quicken each other to what is good, and so help one another to heaven, harden each other in sin, and so ripen one another for hell. To mingle idolatry with Divine worship, and to reject the mediation of Christ, are provoking to God, and ruinous to men. All who worship images, or honour saints, and angels, and the queen of heaven, should recollect what came from the idolatrous practices of the Jews.

Jer. 44:20-30 Whatever evil comes upon us, it is because we have sinned against the Lord; we should therefore stand in awe, and sin not. Since they were determined to persist in their idolatry, God would go on to punish them. What little remains of religion were among them, would be lost. The creature-comforts and confidences from which we promise ourselves most, may fail as soon as those from which we promise ourselves least; and all are what God makes them, not what we fancy them to be. Well-grounded hopes of our having a part in the Divine mercy, are always united with repentance and obedience.
